title_en: COSCO v. Hong Kong Meitong Company and Tianjin Meitong Company — dispute over arrears of ocean freight and port charges

full_text_en:
Tianjin Zhongyuan International Freight Co., Ltd. v. Hong Kong Meitong Shipping Co., Ltd. and Tianjin Meitong International Freight Service Co., Ltd. — dispute over arrears of ocean freight and port charges

Plaintiff: Tianjin Zhongyuan International Freight Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianjin Zhongyuan Company). Domicile: Hebei District, Tianjin.

Legal Representative: Chen Hongsheng, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Fan Xinxin, Staff Member of Tianjin Zhongyuan International Freight Co., Ltd.

Agent ad litem: Hu Zhen, Attorney at Law, Tianjin Hantian Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Yan Ping, Attorney at Law, Tianjin Yuanhai Law Firm.

Defendant: Hong Kong Meitong Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hong Kong Meitong Company). Domicile: Hennessy Road, Hong Kong.

Legal Representative: Zhang Mingkun, General Manager of the Company.

Defendant: Tianjin Meitong International Freight Service Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianjin Meitong Company). Domicile: Heping District, Tianjin.

Legal Representative: Liu Bin, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Xing Yang, Staff Member of Tianjin Meitong International Freight Service Co., Ltd.

The plaintiff, Tianjin Zhongyuan International Freight Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianjin Zhongyuan Company), filed an action with the Tianjin Maritime Court against the defendants, Hong Kong Meitong Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hong Kong Meitong Company) and Tianjin Meitong International Freight Service Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianjin Meitong Company), for a dispute over arrears of ocean freight and port charges.

The plaintiff, Tianjin Zhongyuan Company, alleged: Since 1993, the defendant Hong Kong Meitong Company had entrusted the plaintiff with the transportation of goods, and the plaintiff had actively performed its obligations and delivered the goods to the destinations on time and with quality guaranteed. After the plaintiff performed its obligations, Hong Kong Meitong Company failed to pay on time. As of October 8, 1996, Hong Kong Meitong Company owed the plaintiff freight and port charges equivalent to RMB 4,794,902.30. By the time the plaintiff filed this lawsuit, Hong Kong Meitong Company still owed RMB 4,442,324.11. For the freight and port charges owed by Hong Kong Meitong Company, the defendant Tianjin Meitong Company bore joint and several liability for repayment. To protect the plaintiff's lawful rights and interests, the plaintiff requested the court to order the two defendants to pay the outstanding freight and port charges of RMB 4,442,324.11 in a lump sum and to bear the litigation costs of this case.

The defendants, Hong Kong Meitong Company and Tianjin Meitong Company, did not submit a written defense.

The Tianjin Maritime Court found the following facts through trial:

During the period from 1993 to 1995, the defendant Hong Kong Meitong Company, by entering into separate agreements, entrusted the plaintiff's predecessors, Tianjin Ocean Container Freight Company (hereinafter referred to as Container Company) and Tianjin Ocean Freight Company (hereinafter referred to as Freight Company), with the transportation of goods. The Container Company and the Freight Company, as agreed, safely delivered 218 consignments of goods entrusted by Hong Kong Meitong Company to the destination ports in installments. As of July 2, 1996, Hong Kong Meitong Company owed the Container Company and the Freight Company ocean freight of USD 589,380.71 and port charges of RMB 241,958.01.

The Container Company had, on October 20, 1994, and December 23, 1994, respectively, issued notices for the recovery of overdue payments and notifications of the assertion of rights to the defendant Hong Kong Meitong Company and the defendant Tianjin Meitong Company. In 1995, Hong Kong Meitong Company issued a "Repayment Plan" to the Container Company. The "Repayment Plan" stated: "All ocean freight owed by our company to the Container Company shall be cleared and paid off as soon as possible by June 31, 1995. The monthly repayment shall be approximately USD 100,000 (from March to June 1995)." This "Repayment Plan" was not affixed with the seal of Hong Kong Meitong Company but bore the signature of Zhang Mingkun, the legal representative of Hong Kong Meitong Company, as well as the signature of Liu Bin. At that time, Liu Bin's identity was both an employee of the Tianjin Office of Hong Kong Meitong Company and the legal representative of Tianjin Meitong Company.

From May to October 1996, the defendant Hong Kong Meitong Company, through its Tianjin Office, repaid six installments of freight totaling USD 40,833.21 to the plaintiff Tianjin Zhongyuan Company. From December 17, 1996, to August 21, 1998, the defendant Tianjin Meitong Company repaid to Tianjin Zhongyuan Company six installments of the freight owed by Hong Kong Meitong Company, totaling USD 45,479.30 and RMB 45,542.01. Among these, the freight and document fees of RMB 45,542.01 and USD 3,000 repaid on July 8, 1998, and August 21, 1998, respectively, were paid after Tianjin Meitong Company had learned that Tianjin Zhongyuan Company had filed this lawsuit against it. After deducting the amounts already repaid, Hong Kong Meitong Company still owed Tianjin Zhongyuan Company ocean freight of USD 503,068.20 and port charges of RMB 196,416.10.

It was further discovered: On February 28, 1996, after the Container Company and the Freight Company were dissolved, they were merged to form the plaintiff Tianjin Zhongyuan Company in this case.

The chief representative of the Tianjin Office of the defendant Hong Kong Meitong Company in this case was Su Ziqi. On September 1, 1994, with the approval of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce, Hong Kong Meitong Company established a wholly foreign-owned enterprise in Tianjin — the defendant Tianjin Meitong Company. The business license registration number of this enterprise was 003906, and the legal representative was concurrently held by Liu Bin, an employee of the Tianjin Office of Hong Kong Meitong Company. On April 28, 1996, Hong Kong Meitong Company transferred all its shares in Tianjin Meitong Company to Hong Kong Dapeng Cargo Warehouse Co., Ltd., but the business license, business scope, and legal representative of the enterprise were not changed.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: the freight agreements and bills of lading signed between the Container Company and the Freight Company and the Tianjin Office of Hong Kong Meitong Company; the notices for recovery of overdue payments and notifications of the assertion of rights issued by the Container Company; the "Repayment Plan" issued by Hong Kong Meitong Company; the drafts, checks, and other instruments used by Hong Kong Meitong Company and Tianjin Meitong Company to repay the arrears to Tianjin Zhongyuan Company; the dissolution and merger documents issued by the superior unit of Tianjin Zhongyuan Company; the industrial and commercial registration records at the time of establishment of Tianjin Meitong Company and the business license of the enterprise as a legal person issued by the State Administration for Industry and Commerce; and the documents from the relevant competent authorities approving the change of Tianjin Meitong Company's investor to Hong Kong Dapeng Cargo Company. All evidence, after cross-examination and verification, can be used as the basis for determining the facts of this case.

The Tianjin Maritime Court held: From 1993 to 1995, the entrustment transportation agreements signed between the plaintiff Tianjin Zhongyuan Company and the defendant Hong Kong Meitong Company were legal and valid, and these agreements serve as the basis for determining the rights and obligations between the parties to this case. Tianjin Zhongyuan Company, in accordance with the agreements, had safely delivered all the goods of Hong Kong Meitong Company to the destination ports. After deducting the amounts already repaid, the ocean freight and port charges generated amounted to USD 503,068.20 and RMB 196,416.10, which should still be repaid. Article 88, Paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates: "The parties to a contract shall fully perform their obligations in accordance with the terms of the contract." Hong Kong Meitong Company should, in accordance with the agreements of both parties, repay in full the ocean freight and port charges owed to Tianjin Zhongyuan Company. Article 106, Paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law stipulates: "Citizens and legal persons who breach a contract or fail to perform other obligations shall bear civil liability." Hong Kong Meitong Company's failure to pay the above amounts on time shall bear corresponding civil liability. Although the "Repayment Plan" issued by Hong Kong Meitong Company bore the signature of Liu Bin, the legal representative of the defendant Tianjin Meitong Company, this alone was insufficient to establish that Tianjin Meitong Company bore joint and several liability for the repayment of the debt, as the reasons were insufficient and the evidence was inadequate. Accordingly, the Tianjin Maritime Court rendered the following judgment on January 6, 2000:

The defendant Hong Kong Meitong Company shall repay to the plaintiff Tianjin Zhongyuan Company ocean freight of USD 503,068.20 and port charges of RMB 196,416.10. This amount shall be paid within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment. In case of late payment, the debt interest for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled.

Litigation costs of RMB 38,665.60 shall be borne by the defendant Hong Kong Meitong Company.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, the plaintiff Tianjin Zhongyuan Company, dissatisfied, filed an appeal with the Tianjin High People's Court. The reasons for appeal were: The "Repayment Plan" was not issued solely by the appellee Hong Kong Meitong Company, but was issued jointly by Hong Kong Meitong Company and the appellee Tianjin Meitong Company. Based on the facts that Tianjin Meitong Company confirmed by signing the "Repayment Plan" and subsequently made six installment repayments of the arrears, it was sufficient to establish that Tianjin Meitong Company bore joint and several liability for the debt in this case. Therefore, the debtors in this case should be the two appellees, and a joint and several obligation had been formed between them. The appellant requested the court at second instance to amend the judgment and order Hong Kong Meitong Company to repay ocean freight of USD 503,068.20 and port charges of RMB 196,416.10, and Tianjin Meitong Company to bear joint and several liability for such repayment.

The appellee Hong Kong Meitong Company did not submit a written defense and did not appear in court after a summons was served by public announcement.

The appellee Tianjin Meitong Company did not submit a written defense but argued at the trial: The "Repayment Plan" was an agreement between the appellee Hong Kong Meitong Company and the appellant Tianjin Zhongyuan Company, and there was no third party involved in the agreement. Tianjin Meitong Company made payments directly to Tianjin Zhongyuan Company on behalf of Hong Kong Meitong Company only because it had business dealings with Hong Kong Meitong Company and needed to pay Hong Kong Meitong Company. Since Hong Kong Meitong Company owed fees to Tianjin Zhongyuan Company, to save bank charges, Tianjin Meitong Company paid on behalf of Hong Kong Meitong Company directly to Tianjin Zhongyuan Company. This fact could not prove that Tianjin Meitong Company assumed joint and several liability for the repayment of Hong Kong Meitong Company's arrears.

The Tianjin High People's Court found through trial: The facts found in the first instance were clear and the evidence was sufficient. The freight agreements signed between the appellee Hong Kong Meitong Company and the original Container Company and Freight Company respectively did not violate legal provisions and should be confirmed as valid. The original Container Company and Freight Company had performed their obligations in accordance with the agreements and were entitled to claim ocean freight and port charges from Hong Kong Meitong Company. Article 44, Paragraph 2 of the General Principles of the Civil Law stipulates: "When an enterprise as a legal person is divided or merged, its rights and obligations shall be enjoyed and assumed by the changed legal person." After the Container Company and the Freight Company were dissolved, they were merged to form the appellant Tianjin Zhongyuan Company. Tianjin Zhongyuan Company lawfully enjoyed the creditor's rights left by the Container Company and the Freight Company and was entitled to recover the overdue fees from Hong Kong Meitong Company.

The "Repayment Plan" issued by the appellee Hong Kong Meitong Company, although not affixed with the seal of Hong Kong Meitong Company, bore the signature of Zhang Mingkun, the legal representative of the company, and was legal and valid. The "Repayment Plan" also bore the signature of Liu Bin, who was at that time both an employee of the Tianjin Office of Hong Kong Meitong Company and the legal representative of the appellee Tianjin Meitong Company. When Liu Bin signed, he did not indicate the capacity in which he was signing. The chief representative of the Tianjin Office of Hong Kong Meitong Company was Su Ziqi. At that time, Liu Bin could neither represent the Tianjin Office of Hong Kong Meitong Company nor, even less, represent Hong Kong Meitong Company. Given that the legal representative of Hong Kong Meitong Company had personally signed, if Liu Bin had signed again as an employee of the Tianjin Office of Hong Kong Meitong Company, it would not only be inconsistent with commercial practice but also inconsequential. Therefore, it should be determined that Liu Bin's signature on the "Repayment Plan" was in his capacity as the legal representative of Tianjin Meitong Company. Article 43 of the General Principles of the Civil Law stipulates: "An enterprise as a legal person shall bear civil liability for the business activities of its legal representative and other staff members." Liu Bin's signing of the "Repayment Plan" in his capacity as the legal representative of Tianjin Meitong Company represented Tianjin Meitong Company's confirmation of the "Repayment Plan." This act of confirmation by signature did not involve any coercion, fraud, or material mistake, and was a true expression of Tianjin Meitong Company's voluntary participation in the creditor-debtor relationship between Hong Kong Meitong Company and the original Container Company, with the intention of jointly and severally repaying this debt. Article 54 of the General Principles of the Civil Law stipulates: "A civil juristic act shall be the lawful act of a citizen or legal person to establish, change, or terminate civil rights and obligations." Tianjin Meitong Company's act of confirmation by signature did not violate the law or social public interests and was a lawful act of a legal person to establish civil rights and civil obligations. Therefore, in this case, Tianjin Zhongyuan Company was the creditor, and Hong Kong Meitong Company and Tianjin Meitong Company were joint debtors, with the amount of the debt being all the debts owed by Hong Kong Meitong Company to the original Container Company. This legal relationship between Tianjin Meitong Company and Tianjin Zhongyuan Company was not only confirmed by the signature on the "Repayment Plan" but also by the actual repayment actions of Tianjin Meitong Company. In particular, after Tianjin Zhongyuan Company had already filed this lawsuit against Tianjin Meitong Company in court, Tianjin Meitong Company still made two repayments on July 8, 1998, and August 21, 1998, which further proved that the joint and several repayment liability borne by Tianjin Meitong Company was an objective fact. Tianjin Meitong Company argued that it had made payments to Tianjin Zhongyuan Company on behalf of Hong Kong Meitong Company due to business dealings with Hong Kong Meitong Company and to save bank charges. However, Tianjin Meitong Company could not provide relevant evidence of such business dealings, so this defense could not be established.

The appellee Tianjin Meitong Company only confirmed by signing the "Repayment Plan" issued by the appellee Hong Kong Meitong Company, and the parties did not agree on the respective repayment proportions. In fact, after the "Repayment Plan" was issued, Hong Kong Meitong Company made six repayments of the debt, and Tianjin Meitong Company also made six repayments of the debt. Therefore, Tianjin Meitong Company did not completely replace Hong Kong Meitong Company as the debtor. The above facts prove that Tianjin Meitong Company only joined the creditor-debtor relationship between Hong Kong Meitong Company and the original Container Company as a third party and bore the debt jointly with Hong Kong Meitong Company. The relationship between Hong Kong Meitong Company and Tianjin Meitong Company was one of joint and several liability, and they were joint and several debtors. This case was one of concurrent assumption of debt, not an exemption from debt liability; Hong Kong Meitong Company could not be released from the debt relationship due to Liu Bin's signature on the "Repayment Plan." Although Hong Kong Meitong Company had transferred all its shares in Tianjin Meitong Company to Hong Kong Dapeng Cargo Warehouse Co., Ltd., this was only a change in the investment entity and did not affect Tianjin Meitong Company's independent civil subject status to assume civil rights and obligations. Article 57 of the General Principles of the Civil Law stipulates: "A civil juristic act shall be legally binding from the time of its establishment. The actor shall not alter or rescind it without the provisions of law or the consent of the other party." Tianjin Meitong Company shall continue to bear joint and several liability for the repayment of the amounts owed by Hong Kong Meitong Company to the original Container Company. After Tianjin Meitong Company discharges the debt on behalf of Hong Kong Meitong Company, it shall have the right to seek recourse against Hong Kong Meitong Company.

It should be pointed out that the "Repayment Plan" was issued by the appellee Hong Kong Meitong Company to the original Container Company at the request of the original Container Company. The appellee Tianjin Meitong Company's signature on the "Repayment Plan" only confirmed that it would repay the ocean freight of USD 427,151 owed by Hong Kong Meitong Company to the original Container Company. Tianjin Meitong Company did not bear joint and several liability for the ocean freight of USD 75,917.09 and port charges of RMB 196,416.10 owed by Hong Kong Meitong Company to the original Freight Company.

In summary, the main grounds of appeal of the appellant Tianjin Zhongyuan Company were supported by sufficient evidence and should be upheld, but its request that the appellee Tianjin Meitong Company be jointly and severally liable for the ocean freight and port charges owed by the appellee Hong Kong Meitong Company to the original Freight Company lacked legal basis and should not be supported. The first-instance judgment that Hong Kong Meitong Company bore the repayment liability was correct, but the refusal to order Tianjin Meitong Company to bear partial joint and several liability on the grounds that the evidence for joint and several liability was insufficient was an improper application of law and should be corrected.

Accordingly, the Tianjin High People's Court rendered the following judgment on October 11, 2001:

1. The part of the first-instance civil judgment ordering "Hong Kong Meitong Company to repay to Tianjin Zhongyuan Company ocean freight of USD 503,068.20 and port charges of RMB 196,416.10" is affirmed;

2. The appellee Tianjin Meitong Company shall bear joint and several liability to the appellant Tianjin Zhongyuan Company for the ocean freight of USD 427,151 owed by the appellee Hong Kong Meitong Company to the original Container Company. After Tianjin Meitong Company discharges the debt on behalf of Hong Kong Meitong Company, it shall have the right to seek recourse against Hong Kong Meitong Company;

3. The above payments shall be performed within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment. In case of late payment, the provisions of Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China shall apply.

The first-instance litigation costs shall be borne as per the first-instance judgment; the second-instance litigation costs of RMB 38,665.60 shall be borne by the appellant Tianjin Zhongyuan Company in the amount of RMB 7,733.12 and by the appellee Tianjin Meitong Company in the amount of RMB 30,932.48.
